summary: Iteration 5: retested the 4 fixes from iteration 4. Backend: 14/15 room tests pass (11 in test_rooms_iter4.py plus 3 new in test_rooms_iter5.py, which has 4 tests); the old 51 tests pass. FIX 1: the next turn starts in under 3s after both clients send replay_done, whichever player submits last. Chat sent by the last submitter during resolving is handled right away. In the UI, the time from the last submit to 'Tour: N+1' (this includes the x4 replay) is about 5.7-6.7s, and 'waiting-others' shows briefly. FIX 2: game over takes 3 turns when the guest submits empty programs. Both clients see gameover-banner with 'Vainqueur : Admin'. Only the host sees rematch-btn (the guest's count is 0). Clicking it sends both clients back to room-lobby, and the host sees start-btn. Tested with desktop host and mobile 390px guest. FIX 3: non-JSON text, max_players 'abc'/null and program:5 no longer close the socket; chat and the ready toggle still work and the player stays connected. FIX 4: creating a room from the lobby UI still works. The new catch shows a toast (code review). No page errors. One leftover edge case: a JSON array payload still kills the socket.

minor.issue: A valid JSON message that is not an object (e.g. [1,2,3]) raises AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'. It is raised at msg.get('type') == 'leave', which is outside the inner try, so the socket dies (ConnectionClosedError; seen in backend.err.log). Fix: `if not isinstance(msg, dict): continue` right after receive_json.

issues: When every robot is eliminated in the same turn (draw, winner null), the banner only says 'PARTIE TERMINÉE !' with no 'Égalité/Draw' text. The board is then empty and the host's side panel shows 'Votre robot est éliminé'. Consider a draw label.

action_items: server.py room_ws: skip non-dict JSON messages (isinstance(msg, dict)) so they don't close the socket
Optional: show a draw message in gameover-banner when room.winner is null
critical_code_review_comments: rooms.py: asyncio.create_task(self.resolve()) is fire-and-forget with no reference kept, and its exceptions are not logged. Keep a reference (self._resolve_task) and add a done-callback that logs exceptions
rooms.py _timer also awaits resolve() directly. That is fine because it runs in its own task

success_rate.backend: 93% (14/15 room tests; the only failure is the JSON-array edge case)
